title: From a quiet suburb to the movie capital of the world
lede: Hollywood was named by Daeida Wilcox, whose husband Harvey subdivided a ranch here in 1887 as an orderly, tree-lined suburb. It became a city in 1903, gave up its independence to Los Angeles for water in 1910, and that same decade the filmmakers arrived. Within twenty years the name meant movies everywhere on earth.
tl: Harvey Wilcox files a subdivision map, and his wife Daeida names it Hollywood.
Hollywood merges with Los Angeles to get water.

p: Harvey and Daeida Wilcox subdivided their ranch below the hills in 1887, and Daeida gave it the name Hollywood. It grew into a quiet suburb of orchards and churches, incorporated in 1903, and seven years later voted to join Los Angeles because it needed the city's water.

In 1911 the Nestor company opened the first film studio in Hollywood at Sunset and Gower, and the rest of the industry followed for the sunshine, cheap land and varied scenery. In 1914 Cecil B. DeMille made The Squaw Man in a horse barn near Selma and Vine. That barn, moved twice since, is now the Hollywood Heritage Museum across from the Hollywood Bowl.

ch.h: Palaces, premieres and the Walk of Fame
fact: length of the first Oscars ceremony
p: Showman Sid Grauman built the Egyptian Theatre in 1922 and the Chinese Theatre in 1927, where stars began leaving hand and footprints in the forecourt. The Hollywood Roosevelt opened the same year and hosted the first Academy Awards in 1929, a dinner where the awards took about 15 minutes. Capitol Records finished its round tower in 1956, and the Walk of Fame's first stars went in in 1960.
